description:
FOUND s507 (Fable, 2026-10-05) while taking #2688's fix to main in a fresh scratch worktree (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/wt-m0`, created minutes before; main 6bb94178 + one runtime commit).
MEASURED (logs under ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/m0/ and ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/attrib/):
  the quick companion run in that worktree:        op/die_exit.t DIFF 16/1 (parallel and serial agree)
  the file alone, 25 minutes later, same worktree:  DIFF 6/11 -- rows 7..17 "exit = 0xNN00 bang = … query = …" not ok
  the file alone, twice more, same worktree:        OK 17/0, OK 17/0
  the file alone on main 6bb94178 (twice), on 08de9e4f, and on s507b's worktree (which carries the same runtime commit): OK 17/0 every time
So it is NOT the commit under test: it is the state of a new tree's caches.  Each worktree has its own saved core and its own module-cache key; t/op/die_exit.t runs 17 child programs through the harness, each doing `$! = N; $? = M; die` and asserting the child's exit status.  A child whose run BUILDS a cache entry (or meets one being built) exits with a different status.
CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): in a fresh `git worktree add` of main, run ONE die_exit child by hand twice (`tools/pclperl-for-tests -e '$! = 1; $? = 0; die "x\n"'; echo $?`) with `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1` -- does the first exit status differ from the second, and what did the first run compile (a module? `strict`/`warnings`? the eval cache)?  Then repeat with `PCL_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir>` on an OLD tree: if that reproduces it, the tree is irrelevant and the trigger is any cold module cache.
WHY IT MATTERS: an exit status that depends on whether a cache was warm is a first-run bug users will meet exactly once and never be able to reproduce; and it makes a merge leg run in a fresh worktree report movers that are not there (it cost the #2688 merge an hour of attribution).
Related: #2686 (the cache-building run executes a run-time `require` at compile time; fixed by s507b), #2702 (a used module's print / warn lost on a script's first run), #1338 (the module-cache WRITE-DATE race between trees).
ALSO SEEN, not this task: op/fork.t reads 23/5 alone on 08de9e4f, on main and on the scratch worktree, against its snapshot row 22/6 (and 22/6 inside the s506f companion run): one signal-timing row is load-dependent.
subject: FLAKE with a cause to find (s507): op/die_exit.t fails 1 to 11 of its 17 rows on the FIRST runs in a brand-new worktree (cold caches) and passes 17/0 from then on -- a child's EXIT STATUS on a cache-building run differs from every later run (the "first run is not like later runs" family: #2686, #2702)
